messages:
mikhail: Heads-up: hit a streaming-json parse flake in the JS SDK sample app. When using json_mode + streaming responses, the helper attempts to validate each chunk and throws on the first non-object chunk, causing the request to error and our retry middleware to replay the tool call.

kevin: ouch. streaming should buffer until the final chunk and only validate final assembled JSON. can you paste the chunk log?

mikhail: pasted below. this is from a local repro using the sample tool that streams alternate suggestions as separate chunks. note chunks are valid JSON fragments but not valid top-level objects until combined.

```
stream chunk 1: data: "["
stream chunk 2: data: "{ \"choice\": \"A\" },"
stream chunk 3: data: "{ \"choice\": \"B\" }"
stream chunk 4: data: "]"
stream done
```

mikhail: The helper calls validateStrict on each chunk which fails on chunk 1 (it expects object). That triggers an Error thrown inside the streaming parser. Our auth/retry middleware sees an exception thrown during response handling and retries the whole request which causes the tool to run twice. That double-run breaks idempotency and the sample-app side-effect (writes to a mock DB) occurs twice.

tanya: Are other SDKs doing the same? Python streams usually buffer then yield parsed objects. We've got a parity gap.

kevin: We intentionally allowed chunk-level parsing for some non-JSON streams (plain text), but clearly for json_mode we should treat stream as framed JSON and assemble until we have a complete JSON value before validating. Two fixes: (1) change JS helper to accumulate tokens/fragments until full JSON parse succeeds; (2) treat parse-time ValidationError as non-retryable so we don't replay side-effectful tool calls.

mikhail: I prefer the assemble approach as default and an escape hatch flag `validate_on_chunk=true` for advanced use. Also add `streaming_json_mode: 'buffered' | 'incremental'` option so apps that actually need incremental validation can opt in. Default to 'buffered'.

kevin: Agree. For retries: middleware currently catches any thrown error during response handling and retries if it's not an explicit 4xx from the network. We should map runtime parse errors to `INVALID_SCHEMA` with a 4xx classification.

qa-bot: [test-run] reproduced in CI: sdk-js e2e stream-json flake on macos-latest (job #452). Failure: parse error on first chunk -> retry -> duplicate DB row.

mikhail: Plan to open a PR that: 
- buffers stream payloads for json_mode by default and validates after full JSON assembly
- adds `streaming_json_mode` client option and docs for incremental parsing
- introduce ValidationError subclass with `code: INVALID_SCHEMA` to prevent retries
- add e2e test that mocks streaming chunks and asserts only single tool invocation

tanya: add a note in sample-app README about streaming vs non-streaming tool contracts. Recommend: if tool emits multiple independent JSON objects, wrap them in an envelope `{ variants: [...] }` or use line-delimited JSON and set `streaming_json_mode: 'incremental'`.

kevin: Also ensure the telemetry/metrics don't count the thrown client-side parse error as a server-side retryable fault. We have an open metric for "server_retries" that skews SLOs.

mikhail: PR incoming: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/901. tagging @devex @eng-runtime. Will include unit+e2e and README updates.

kevin: thanks — lgtm once tests pass.

mikhail: Thanks all :sparkles:
